instructions: The night before, or at least 3 hours ahead: Put the pork belly in a medium pot, cover it with cold water, and bring it to a boil over high heat. When the outside turns opaque, after about 3 minutes, turn off the heat.
Transfer the pork to a bowl and rinse it under running water. Rinse out the pot.

Return the pork to the clean pot. Add 1 cup water, the Shaoxing wine, sugar, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, 2 scallions cut in half, the ginger, star anise, cinnamon stick, cardamom pod, Sichuan peppercorns and bay leaf. Bring to a boil.
Turn the heat to low and simmer for 1 hour 30 minutes, until a fork slides in and out easily. Keep the heat low so the sauce doesn't boil away. Taste the sauce and add a pinch of salt if it's flat.
Let the pork cool in its sauce. Cover and refrigerate for up to 4 days.
In a large bowl, stir together the flour, yeast and 1/4 tsp salt. Add 1/3 cup warm water a little at a time, stirring until a smooth dough comes together. If it's dry, add another tbsp of warm water.
Knead the dough on the counter for 10 minutes, until smooth and springy. Cover it with a towel and let it sit at room temperature for 1 hour, until doubled.

Punch the dough down and knead it for 1 minute. Cut it into 4 equal pieces. Roll each into a long strip, fold it in half lengthwise, roll it up into a coil, and press it flat into a disc about 4 inches across. Cover with a towel and let the discs sit for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, warm the pork and its sauce in the pot over medium-low heat for 10 minutes. Transfer the pork to a cutting board and chop it coarsely. Chop 1/4 cup of the cilantro.
Mix the chopped pork with the cilantro and 1/4 cup of the braising liquid in a bowl. Keep the rest of the sauce warm on low heat.
Heat a dry flat skillet over medium heat. Add 2 of the discs, cover, and cook 2 minutes per side. Uncover and cook about 1 minute per side, until golden. Repeat with the other 2 discs.
Split each one open and pile in the pork. Serve with the rest of the warm sauce in a small bowl.

Leftover pork keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days. Reheat it in a pot over medium-low heat with a splash of water. Wrap any leftover flatbreads in a zip-top bag for 2 days and warm them in a dry skillet.
advance_prep_notes: braise the pork the night before (or at least 3 hours ahead)
method_notes: The Woks of Life version (4.91 from 40) leads. It blanches the pork belly, braises it low for 90 minutes to 2 hours in Shaoxing wine, soy, rock sugar and whole spices, and says to braise it a day ahead. The bun is a plain yeast dough cooked in a dry covered skillet. Its recipe makes 12, so everything here is cut to a third for 4. Galangal is left out and the spices trimmed to suit a smaller pot. The braise is the long part, which is why it is set as a make-ahead first step.
